chunks: As for what Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad narrated from Saʿd ibn Ismāʿīl, from his father Ismāʿīl ibn ʿĪsā, who said:

I asked al-Riḍā عليه السلام about a man who performs the first prayer, then performs supererogatory prayer, and the time of ʿaṣr comes upon him before he finishes his nafilah. Should he delay ʿaṣr and complete his nafilah, or perform it after ʿaṣr, or postpone it until he performs it at another time? He said: "He should perform ʿaṣr and make up his nafilah on another day."

The interpretation of this report is that if he were to pray at the end of the time, he would be nearing the setting of the sun, and that is a time in which prayer is disliked, as we have clarified in most narrations. So it is preferable that he postpone it and make it up at another time.

key_terms.الْعَصْرِ: the obligatory ʿaṣr salat (prayer), whose time has entered
key_terms.غَيْبُوبَةَ الشَّمْسِ: the setting or disappearance of the sun near sunset
key_terms.نَافِلَتِهِ: his supererogatory prayer performed in addition to the obligatory salat (prayer)
key_terms.وَقْتٍ آخَرَ: another time in which the delayed prayer may be made up
key_terms.يَقْضِي: he makes up or performs later what was missed
key_terms.يُكْرَهُ: it is considered disliked or discouraged in legal terms

ai.seo_question: What should someone do if the time of ʿaṣr begins before finishing a nafilah prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning the conflict between the time of ʿaṣr salat (prayer) and a supererogatory nafilah prayer. It instructs that the obligatory ʿaṣr salat (prayer) takes priority, while the nafilah should be made up later, especially since delaying into the period near sunset is considered disliked for prayer.
